Subject: DBMS
Question: Which of the following best describes an entity in the ER model?
Option2: A property that describes another object
Option3: A thing or object in the real world with an independent existence
Option4: A named column of a relational table
CorrectAnswer: A thing or object in the real world with an independent existence
Explanation: An entity is a real-world thing, physical or conceptual, that exists independently and is represented in the database.

Subject: DBMS
Question: A collection of entities that all have the same attributes is called an:
CorrectAnswer: Entity type
Explanation: An entity type defines a collection of entities sharing the same attributes, and its schema is described by its name and attributes.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In the ER model, an attribute represents:
Option1: A collection of entities of the same kind
Option2: A property that describes an entity
Option4: A constraint on the number of participating entities
CorrectAnswer: A property that describes an entity
Explanation: Attributes are the particular properties, such as Name or Salary, that describe an entity.

Subject: DBMS
Question: An attribute that cannot be divided into smaller meaningful components is called a:
CorrectAnswer: Simple (atomic) attribute
Explanation: A simple attribute is atomic, whereas a composite attribute can be divided into subparts.

Subject: DBMS
Question: An Address attribute made up of Street, City, State and Zip is an example of a:
CorrectAnswer: Composite attribute
Explanation: A composite attribute is formed from several simple component attributes.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Which of the following is the most natural multivalued attribute of a PERSON entity?
Option1: College_degrees, since a person may hold several degrees
CorrectAnswer: College_degrees, since a person may hold several degrees
Explanation: A multivalued attribute can hold more than one value for a single entity, such as several college degrees.

Subject: DBMS
Question: An attribute such as Age, whose value can be computed from Birth_date and the current date, is called a:
CorrectAnswer: Derived attribute
Explanation: A derived attribute is one whose value is obtained from another stored attribute or from related entities.

Subject: DBMS
Question: An attribute whose value is unique for each entity in an entity set is called a:
CorrectAnswer: Key attribute
Explanation: A key attribute has distinct values for every entity, so it can be used to identify entities uniquely.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In Elmasri and Navathe's ER diagram notation, an entity type is drawn as a:
CorrectAnswer: Rectangle
Explanation: Entity types are shown as rectangular boxes labeled with the entity type name.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In ER diagram notation, a relationship type is drawn as a:
CorrectAnswer: Diamond
Explanation: Relationship types are shown as diamond-shaped boxes connected to the participating entity types.

Subject: DBMS
Question: How is a key attribute indicated in Elmasri and Navathe's ER diagram notation?
Option3: It is connected with a dashed line
Option4: It is drawn as a double oval
CorrectAnswer: Its name is underlined
Explanation: Key attributes have their names underlined inside the attribute oval.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In ER diagrams, a multivalued attribute is drawn as a:
Option1: Oval connected by a double line
CorrectAnswer: Double oval
Explanation: A double-lined oval marks an attribute that can hold multiple values per entity.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In ER diagrams, a weak entity type is drawn as a:
CorrectAnswer: Double rectangle
Explanation: A double-lined rectangle distinguishes a weak entity type from an ordinary entity type.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In ER diagrams, total participation of an entity type in a relationship type is shown by a:
Option2: Double line connecting the entity type to the relationship
Option4: Line labeled with the letter N
CorrectAnswer: Double line connecting the entity type to the relationship
Explanation: A double line indicates that every entity of that type must participate in the relationship.

Subject: DBMS
Question: The number of entity types that participate in a relationship type is called its:
CorrectAnswer: Degree
Explanation: The degree of a relationship type is the count of participating entity types, for example 2 for a binary relationship.

Subject: DBMS
Question: A relationship type that involves exactly two entity types is called:
CorrectAnswer: Binary relationship
Explanation: A relationship of degree two is called binary.

Subject: DBMS
Question: A relationship type in which the same entity type participates more than once in different roles is called:
CorrectAnswer: Recursive (unary) relationship
Explanation: In a recursive relationship, such as SUPERVISION on EMPLOYEE, one entity type plays several roles.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In a recursive relationship such as SUPERVISION on EMPLOYEE, what is used to distinguish the two participations of EMPLOYEE?
Option1: Role names such as supervisor and supervisee
CorrectAnswer: Role names such as supervisor and supervisee
Explanation: Role names specify the function each participating entity plays in the relationship.

Subject: DBMS
Question: The cardinality ratio of a binary relationship type specifies:
Option1: The number of entity types in the relationship
Option2: The maximum number of relationship instances in which an entity can participate
Option3: The number of attributes the relationship has
Option4: Whether every entity must participate in the relationship
CorrectAnswer: The maximum number of relationship instances in which an entity can participate
Explanation: Cardinality ratio is a structural constraint giving the maximum number of related entities on each side.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Which of the following lists all the possible cardinality ratios for a binary relationship type?
CorrectAnswer: 1:1, 1:N, N:1 and M:N
Explanation: The four possible cardinality ratios of a binary relationship are 1:1, 1:N, N:1 and M:N.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Total participation of an entity type in a relationship type means that:
Option1: Some entities of that type may not participate
Option2: The relationship type has no attributes
Option3: Every entity of that type must be related to at least one entity through the relationship
Option4: Each entity participates in exactly one relationship instance
CorrectAnswer: Every entity of that type must be related to at least one entity through the relationship
Explanation: Total participation, also called existence dependency, requires every entity to appear in some relationship instance.

Subject: DBMS
Question: A weak entity type is one that:
Option1: Has no relationship with any other entity type
Option3: Cannot participate in any relationship type
Option4: Has no key attribute of its own and depends on an owner entity type for identification
CorrectAnswer: Has no key attribute of its own and depends on an owner entity type for identification
Explanation: Weak entities are identified by being related to an owner (strong) entity, and they lack their own key.

Subject: DBMS
Question: The relationship type that relates a weak entity type to its owner entity type is called the:
CorrectAnswer: Identifying relationship
Explanation: The identifying relationship connects a weak entity type to the owner that identifies it.

Subject: DBMS
Question: The attribute that uniquely identifies weak entities among those related to the same owner entity is called the:
CorrectAnswer: Partial key (discriminator)
Explanation: A partial key distinguishes weak entities only within the set related to one owner entity.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In EER modeling, a subclass is:
Option2: A subgrouping of the entities of another entity type (the superclass) that has meaningful distinct attributes or relationships
Option3: A derived attribute of the superclass
Option4: A relationship type between two entity types
CorrectAnswer: A subgrouping of the entities of another entity type (the superclass) that has meaningful distinct attributes or relationships
Explanation: A subclass is a meaningful subset of a superclass's entities that needs to be represented explicitly.

Subject: DBMS
Question: The process of defining a set of subclasses of an entity type is called:
CorrectAnswer: Specialization
Explanation: Specialization is the top-down process of defining subclasses based on distinguishing characteristics.

Subject: DBMS
Question: A subclass entity inherits which of the following from its superclass?
Option1: All attributes and relationships of the superclass
Option2: Nothing, because the subclass is defined independently
Option3: Only the relationships, not the attributes
Option4: Only the key attributes of the superclass
CorrectAnswer: All attributes and relationships of the superclass
Explanation: Attribute and relationship inheritance means a subclass member has everything the superclass member has.

Subject: DBMS
Question: The ER model is mainly used for:
CorrectAnswer: Conceptual design of a database
Explanation: The ER model is a high-level conceptual data model used to design database structure before implementation.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Which situation justifies assigning a NULL value to an attribute?
Option1: The attribute is a composite attribute
Option2: The attribute is a derived attribute
Option3: The attribute does not apply to that entity, for example Apartment_number for a detached house
Option4: The attribute is a key attribute
CorrectAnswer: The attribute does not apply to that entity, for example Apartment_number for a detached house
Explanation: NULL represents a value that is not applicable, unknown or missing for a particular entity.

Subject: DBMS
Question: The set of values that may be assigned to an attribute is called its:
CorrectAnswer: Value set (domain)
Explanation: The value set, or domain, specifies which values are permitted for an attribute of each entity.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Each department has many employees, but each employee works for exactly one department. What is the cardinality ratio DEPARTMENT:EMPLOYEE of the WORKS_FOR relationship?
Explanation: One department relates to many employees, whereas each employee relates to only one department.

Subject: DBMS
Question: A student can enroll in many courses and a course can have many students. What is the cardinality ratio of the ENROLLS relationship?
CorrectAnswer: M:N
Explanation: Both sides can be related to many entities of the other type, which gives an M:N ratio.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Each department has exactly one manager, and an employee can manage at most one department. What is the cardinality ratio of the MANAGES relationship?
Explanation: Each entity on either side is related to at most one entity on the other side.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In a 1:N relationship WORKS_FOR between DEPARTMENT (1 side) and EMPLOYEE (N side), the relationship attribute Start_date can instead be placed on:
Option1: The EMPLOYEE entity type (the N side)
Option2: Neither, since it must stay on the relationship
CorrectAnswer: The EMPLOYEE entity type (the N side)
Explanation: In a 1:N relationship each N-side entity has at most one related entity, so the attribute can migrate to the N side.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In an M:N relationship WORKS_ON between EMPLOYEE and PROJECT, the attribute Hours (hours per week an employee works on a project) must be placed on:
Option3: Either entity type, whichever is more convenient
CorrectAnswer: The relationship type
Explanation: Hours depends on the combination of an employee and a project, so it cannot belong to either entity alone.

Subject: DBMS
Question: DEPENDENT is a weak entity type identified by its owner EMPLOYEE (key Ssn) and a partial key Dependent_name. What is the full identifier of a DEPENDENT entity?
Option1: The name of the identifying relationship
CorrectAnswer: Ssn together with Dependent_name
Explanation: A weak entity is identified by the owner's key combined with its own partial key.

Subject: DBMS
Question: What kind of participation must a weak entity type have in its identifying relationship?
CorrectAnswer: Total participation
Explanation: A weak entity cannot exist without its owner, so it must participate totally in the identifying relationship.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In the (min,max) notation, an EMPLOYEE entity type is labeled (0,1) in the MANAGES relationship type. This means:
Option1: Every employee manages exactly one department
Option2: Every employee manages at least one department
Option3: An employee may manage many departments
Option4: An employee manages at most one department and may manage none
CorrectAnswer: An employee manages at most one department and may manage none
Explanation: Min 0 means partial participation and max 1 limits each employee to at most one MANAGES instance.

Subject: DBMS
Question: The Dept attribute of STUDENT is later found to have its own attributes and to take part in other relationships. What is the best refinement of the design?
Option3: Make Dept a weak entity type of STUDENT
Option4: Convert the attribute into a DEPARTMENT entity type related to STUDENT by a relationship type
CorrectAnswer: Convert the attribute into a DEPARTMENT entity type related to STUDENT by a relationship type
Explanation: An attribute that acquires its own structure and relationships should be promoted to an entity type.

Subject: DBMS
Question: How is a composite attribute represented in an ER diagram?
Option1: As an oval connected to the ovals of its component attributes
Option4: As an oval joined to the entity by a double line
CorrectAnswer: As an oval connected to the ovals of its component attributes
Explanation: A composite attribute is drawn with its component attributes hanging from it as ovals.

Subject: DBMS
Question: How is a derived attribute shown in an ER diagram?
Option2: As an oval with a double line
CorrectAnswer: As a dashed oval
Explanation: Derived attributes are drawn with dashed outlines to show they are not stored independently.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In Elmasri and Navathe's notation, {Address_phone({Phone(Area_code, Phone_number)}, Address(Street_address(Number, Street, Apartment_number), City, State, Zip))} represents:
Option3: A complex attribute formed by nesting composite and multivalued attributes
CorrectAnswer: A complex attribute formed by nesting composite and multivalued attributes
Explanation: Braces denote multivalued components and parentheses denote composite components, and nesting them gives a complex attribute.

Subject: DBMS
Question: A CAR entity type has two attributes that are each unique: Vehicle_id, and the pair (State, Reg_number). Which statement is correct?
Option1: CAR must be a weak entity type
Option2: CAR has only one key because Vehicle_id makes the pair redundant
Option3: The ER model allows only one key attribute per entity type
Option4: CAR has two candidate keys, one of which is composite
CorrectAnswer: CAR has two candidate keys, one of which is composite
Explanation: An entity type can have more than one key, and a key can consist of several attributes.

Subject: DBMS
Question: How is an identifying relationship type drawn in an ER diagram?
Option1: As a rectangle with double lines
Option2: As a diamond with dashed lines
Option3: As a diamond with an underlined name
CorrectAnswer: As a double diamond
Explanation: The double diamond distinguishes the identifying relationship of a weak entity type.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In the SUPERVISION relationship on EMPLOYEE, the top executive has no supervisor. What does this imply?
Option1: EMPLOYEE participates totally in the supervisee role
Option2: EMPLOYEE participates partially in the supervisee role
Option3: EMPLOYEE must be a weak entity type
CorrectAnswer: EMPLOYEE participates partially in the supervisee role
Explanation: Because some employee is not a supervisee, participation in that role is partial.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Combining several entity types with common features into a single superclass is called:
CorrectAnswer: Generalization
Explanation: Generalization is the bottom-up process that suppresses differences and abstracts common features into a superclass.

Subject: DBMS
Question: SECRETARY, TECHNICIAN and ENGINEER are subclasses of EMPLOYEE, and membership is determined by the value of the Job_type attribute. This specialization is:
CorrectAnswer: Attribute-defined
Explanation: When all subclass membership conditions test the same attribute, the specialization is attribute-defined.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Membership in a subclass is decided by database users when they assign entities, rather than by a condition on attributes. Such a subclass is:
CorrectAnswer: User-defined
Explanation: User-defined subclasses have no membership condition, so users specify membership when adding entities.

Subject: DBMS
Question: The disjointness constraint (marked d) on a specialization means:
Option1: An entity can be a member of at most one of the subclasses
Option2: Every superclass entity must belong to some subclass
Option3: A subclass entity must belong to all its superclasses
Option4: The subclasses cannot have attributes of their own
CorrectAnswer: An entity can be a member of at most one of the subclasses
Explanation: A disjoint specialization forbids an entity from belonging to more than one subclass.

Subject: DBMS
Question: A total specialization (drawn with a double line) means that:
Option1: An entity can belong to at most one subclass
Option3: The superclass has no entities of its own
Option4: Every entity in the superclass must be a member of at least one subclass
CorrectAnswer: Every entity in the superclass must be a member of at least one subclass
Explanation: Total specialization is the completeness constraint requiring each superclass entity to appear in a subclass.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Because disjointness (disjoint or overlapping) and completeness (total or partial) are independent, how many combinations of specialization constraints are possible?
CorrectAnswer: Four
Explanation: The four combinations are disjoint total, disjoint partial, overlapping total and overlapping partial.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In a specialization hierarchy, each subclass:
Option1: Can have more than one superclass (multiple inheritance)
Option2: Must belong to a total specialization
Option3: Cannot have subclasses of its own
Option4: Participates as a subclass in only one class/subclass relationship (single inheritance)
CorrectAnswer: Participates as a subclass in only one class/subclass relationship (single inheritance)
Explanation: A hierarchy has a tree structure with single inheritance, unlike a lattice where a subclass may have several superclasses.

Subject: DBMS
Question: ENGINEERING_MANAGER is a shared subclass of ENGINEER and MANAGER. Every member of ENGINEERING_MANAGER must be:
Option1: A member of both ENGINEER and MANAGER
Option2: A member of either ENGINEER or MANAGER
Option3: A member of neither, since it is a separate entity type
CorrectAnswer: A member of both ENGINEER and MANAGER
Explanation: A shared subclass is a subset of the intersection of its superclasses.

Subject: DBMS
Question: OWNER is modeled as a subclass of the union of PERSON, BANK and COMPANY. Such a subclass is called a:
CorrectAnswer: Category (union type)
Explanation: A category represents entities drawn from the union of different entity types.

Subject: DBMS
Question: An entity that belongs to a subclass of EMPLOYEE such as SECRETARY represents:
Option1: A different entity that duplicates the superclass member
Option2: A relationship instance between two employees
Option3: A weak entity identified by the superclass member
Option4: The same real-world entity as a member of the superclass, playing a distinct specific role
CorrectAnswer: The same real-world entity as a member of the superclass, playing a distinct specific role
Explanation: A subclass member is the same entity as the corresponding superclass member, viewed in a specific role.

Subject: DBMS
Question: The attribute Typing_speed applies only to the SECRETARY subclass of EMPLOYEE. In EER terms it is a:
CorrectAnswer: Specific (local) attribute of the subclass
Explanation: A subclass can have specific attributes in addition to those it inherits.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In Silberschatz et al.'s ER notation, treating a relationship set as an abstract entity so that it can take part in another relationship is called:
CorrectAnswer: Aggregation
Explanation: Aggregation abstracts a relationship into a higher-level entity that can participate in further relationships.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In Silberschatz et al.'s notation, a directed line (arrow) from a relationship set to an entity set indicates that the entity set:
Option1: Participates in at most one instance of that relationship (the 'one' side)
CorrectAnswer: Participates in at most one instance of that relationship (the 'one' side)
Explanation: An arrow toward an entity set marks the 'one' side, so each such entity is related to at most one other entity.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In Silberschatz et al.'s l..h notation, the label 0..* next to an entity set in a relationship means:
Option1: It participates in at most one relationship instance
Option2: It participates in exactly one relationship instance
Option3: The entity set may participate in zero or many relationship instances
Option4: It participates in at least one relationship instance
CorrectAnswer: The entity set may participate in zero or many relationship instances
Explanation: The lower limit 0 allows non-participation and the upper limit * places no bound on participation.

Subject: DBMS
Question: For a 1:1 relationship type MANAGES with the attribute Start_date, where can the attribute be placed?
Option1: Only on the entity type with partial participation
Option3: Only on the entity type with total participation
Option4: It can be migrated to either participating entity type
CorrectAnswer: It can be migrated to either participating entity type
Explanation: In a 1:1 relationship, each entity has at most one partner, so the attribute can move to either entity type.

Subject: DBMS
Question: A ternary relationship SUPPLY among SUPPLIER, PART and PROJECT is replaced by three binary relationships (CAN_SUPPLY, USES, SUPPLIES). Which statement is correct?
Option1: The binary versions are not equivalent in general, because they cannot record which supplier supplies which part to which project
Option2: They are equivalent only if all three participations are total
Option3: They are equivalent only if the relationship is M:N:N
Option4: They are always equivalent, so the ternary relationship is unnecessary
CorrectAnswer: The binary versions are not equivalent in general, because they cannot record which supplier supplies which part to which project
Explanation: A ternary relationship captures combinations of three entities that three binary relationships cannot reconstruct without spurious facts.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Relationship R between A and B has cardinality ratio A:B = 1:N, and B participates totally. If |A| = 8 and |B| = 20, how many relationship instances exist?
Explanation: Each B entity is related to exactly one A entity, so there are exactly 20 relationship instances.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Relationship R between A and B is M:N with |A| = 6 and |B| = 5. What is the maximum possible number of relationship instances?
Explanation: Each (a, b) pair can appear at most once, so the maximum is 6 x 5 = 30.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Relationship R between A and B is 1:1 with total participation of both A and B. If |A| = 12, then |B| is:
Explanation: Total participation with a 1:1 ratio pairs each A with exactly one B, forming a one-to-one correspondence.

Subject: DBMS
Question: EMPLOYEE has 50 entities. In the recursive SUPERVISION relationship, every employee except the CEO has exactly one supervisor. How many relationship instances exist?
Explanation: Each of the 49 supervised employees participates in exactly one SUPERVISION instance.

Subject: DBMS
Question: ROOM is a weak entity type of BUILDING (partial key Room_no), and BED is a weak entity type of ROOM (partial key Bed_no). Which attributes together identify a BED?
CorrectAnswer: Building key, Room_no and Bed_no
Explanation: Identification chains through each owner, so the full key combines the strong entity key and all partial keys.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Can a weak entity type have more than one owner (identifying) entity type?
Option1: No, a weak entity type has exactly one owner
Option2: Yes, it can be identified by a combination of several owner entity types through an n-ary identifying relationship
Option3: Only if the owners are related to each other
Option4: Only if it has a key of its own
CorrectAnswer: Yes, it can be identified by a combination of several owner entity types through an n-ary identifying relationship
Explanation: A weak entity may depend on several entity types together, and their keys jointly contribute to its identifier.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Under what condition can a weak entity type such as DEPENDENT be modeled as a complex (multivalued composite) attribute of its owner?
Option1: When its participation in the identifying relationship is partial
Option2: When it takes part in no relationship types other than its identifying relationship
Option3: When it has a key of its own
Option4: When the owner entity type is also weak
CorrectAnswer: When it takes part in no relationship types other than its identifying relationship
Explanation: If the weak entity participates independently in other relationships, it must remain a separate entity type.

Subject: DBMS
Question: The multivalued attribute Color of CAR is given lower and upper bounds (1,3). This means:
Option2: Cars may have between 1 and 3 keys
Option3: Every car has at least 1 and at most 3 color values
Option4: Color values must lie between 1 and 3
CorrectAnswer: Every car has at least 1 and at most 3 color values
Explanation: The bounds constrain how many values the multivalued attribute may hold per entity.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In an attribute-defined specialization, each subclass has a membership condition of the form Job_type = value. If the defining attribute is single-valued, the subclasses must be:
CorrectAnswer: Disjoint
Explanation: A single-valued attribute cannot equal two different values at once, so an entity cannot satisfy two conditions.

Subject: DBMS
Question: OWNER is a category (union type) of PERSON, BANK and COMPANY. Which inheritance applies to a member of OWNER?
Option2: Selective inheritance: it inherits the attributes of only the superclass to which it belongs
Option3: Multiple inheritance from all three superclasses
CorrectAnswer: Selective inheritance: it inherits the attributes of only the superclass to which it belongs
Explanation: Members of a category belong to just one of the defining superclasses and inherit only from that one.

Subject: DBMS
Question: A category (union type) is total when:
Option1: It contains the union of all entities of its defining superclasses
Option2: It allows at most one superclass
Option3: It has no attributes of its own
Option4: It contains only the entities common to all superclasses
CorrectAnswer: It contains the union of all entities of its defining superclasses
Explanation: A total category holds every entity of every defining superclass, whereas a partial category holds only a subset.

Subject: DBMS
Question: PERSON, BANK and COMPANY have different keys (Ssn, Bank_name, Company_id). Which attribute typically identifies the entities of the category OWNER?
Option3: Any of the three keys, chosen by the DBMS
Option4: A new surrogate key attribute such as Owner_id
CorrectAnswer: A new surrogate key attribute such as Owner_id
Explanation: Because the superclasses have different keys, the category needs its own surrogate key.

Subject: DBMS
Question: A specialization of EMPLOYEE into {SECRETARY, TECHNICIAN, ENGINEER} is declared total and disjoint. A janitor is stored in EMPLOYEE but in none of the subclasses. Is this consistent?
Option1: Yes, because a janitor is a weak entity
Option2: No, because the janitor would then have to belong to all subclasses
Option3: Yes, because disjointness allows an entity to belong to no subclass
Option4: No, total specialization requires every employee to belong to at least one subclass
CorrectAnswer: No, total specialization requires every employee to belong to at least one subclass
Explanation: A total constraint forbids superclass entities that belong to no subclass.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In relationship R between A and B, A is labeled (1,N) and B is labeled (0,1) in (min,max) notation. Which statement is correct?
Option1: A:B = 1:N, with total participation of A and partial participation of B
Option2: A:B = 1:N, with partial participation of A and total participation of B
Option3: A:B = M:N, with partial participation of both
Option4: A:B = N:1, with total participation of A and partial participation of B
CorrectAnswer: A:B = 1:N, with total participation of A and partial participation of B
Explanation: B's max of 1 means each B relates to at most one A, and A's min of 1 makes A total while B's min of 0 makes it partial.

Subject: DBMS
Question: An employee may work on the same project several times in separate stints, but a relationship set cannot contain the same (employee, project) pair twice. Which is a suitable modeling approach?
Option1: Add a derived attribute to PROJECT
Option4: Model each stint as an entity type (for example a weak entity or one with a Stint_no) linked to EMPLOYEE and PROJECT
CorrectAnswer: Model each stint as an entity type (for example a weak entity or one with a Stint_no) linked to EMPLOYEE and PROJECT
Explanation: Since instances must be unique, repeated associations need an extra identifying element such as a stint entity.

Subject: DBMS
Question: A PART may be made up of other PARTs, and a PART may be used in many other PARTs (bill of materials). Which relationship type models this?
Option2: A recursive M:N relationship on PART
Option3: A ternary relationship among PART, PART and PART
Option4: A weak entity type of PART
CorrectAnswer: A recursive M:N relationship on PART
Explanation: Each part can contain many parts and be contained in many parts, so the recursive relationship is M:N.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In an M:N relationship between A (key a_id) and B (key b_id), a relationship instance is uniquely identified by:
Option1: A separate system-generated attribute of the relationship
Option3: The combination of a_id and b_id
CorrectAnswer: The combination of a_id and b_id
Explanation: A relationship instance is defined by the participating entities, so their combined keys identify it.

Subject: DBMS
Question: PERSON is specialized into EMPLOYEE, ALUMNUS and STUDENT. A person may belong to several of these, and some persons belong to none. What are the constraints?
CorrectAnswer: Overlapping and partial
Explanation: Membership in several subclasses means overlapping, and persons outside every subclass means partial.

Subject: DBMS
Question: ENGINEERING_MANAGER is a shared subclass of ENGINEER and MANAGER, which are both subclasses of EMPLOYEE. How many times does ENGINEERING_MANAGER inherit the attributes of EMPLOYEE?
Option1: Once, because they are the same attributes reached through two inheritance paths
Option4: Never, since only direct superclasses count
CorrectAnswer: Once, because they are the same attributes reached through two inheritance paths
Explanation: The attributes of a common ancestor are inherited once even if reached through multiple paths.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In a ternary relationship R among A, B and C, the cardinality label on C is 1 (with N on A and N on B). What does this mean?
Option1: For each combination of an A entity and a B entity, at most one C entity is related
Option2: Each C entity is related to at most one (A, B) pair
Option3: Each A entity is related to exactly one C entity
Option4: Each C entity is related to at most one A entity
CorrectAnswer: For each combination of an A entity and a B entity, at most one C entity is related
Explanation: In an n-ary relationship, a 1 on one participant limits it for each combination of the other participants.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Which kind of attribute cannot serve as a key attribute of an entity type?
CorrectAnswer: A multivalued attribute
Explanation: A key must give exactly one identifying value per entity, which a multivalued attribute cannot do.

Subject: DBMS
Question: An ER diagram has entity types A, B and C. A:B is 1:N and B:C is M:N. What is the minimum number of tables needed in the resulting relational schema?
Explanation: Each entity type gets a table, the 1:N relationship uses a foreign key in B, and the M:N relationship needs its own table.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Which statement about participation and weak entity types is TRUE?
Option1: Every entity type with total participation is a weak entity type
Option2: An entity type can participate totally in a relationship without being a weak entity type
Option3: A weak entity type has partial participation in its identifying relationship
Option4: A weak entity type must have a primary key of its own
CorrectAnswer: An entity type can participate totally in a relationship without being a weak entity type
Explanation: For example, EMPLOYEE participates totally in WORKS_FOR yet has its own key and is a strong entity type.

Subject: DBMS
Question: EMPLOYEE and DEPARTMENT are related by both WORKS_FOR and MANAGES. Is it valid to have two relationship types between the same pair of entity types?
Option1: Only if both have the same cardinality ratio
Option2: Yes, provided the relationship types have different names and meanings, and possibly different constraints
Option3: Only if one of the entity types is weak
Option4: No, only one relationship type is allowed between two entity types
CorrectAnswer: Yes, provided the relationship types have different names and meanings, and possibly different constraints
Explanation: Different associations between the same entity types are modeled as distinct relationship types.

Question: Relationship R between A and B is M:N with total participation of both. If |A| = 5 and |B| = 8, what is the minimum number of relationship instances?
Explanation: Every B needs at least one instance, and the 5 A entities can be covered within those 8 instances.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Which of the following is best modeled with specialization (IS-A) rather than an ordinary relationship type?
Option1: A MANAGER is a kind of EMPLOYEE with extra attributes
Option2: An EMPLOYEE works for a DEPARTMENT
Option4: A STUDENT enrolls in a COURSE
CorrectAnswer: A MANAGER is a kind of EMPLOYEE with extra attributes
Explanation: An IS-A association where one type is a special kind of another with extra properties calls for a subclass.

Subject: DBMS
Question: In Silberschatz et al.'s ER notation, how is specialization (ISA) shown?
Option2: By a hollow-headed arrow from the specialized entity set to the more general entity set
Option4: By a double line to the superclass
CorrectAnswer: By a hollow-headed arrow from the specialized entity set to the more general entity set
Explanation: The ISA relationship is drawn with a hollow arrowhead pointing to the higher-level entity set.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Two entity types A and B are related 1:1 with total participation on both sides. Which design option is possible?
Option1: Replace the relationship with a ternary relationship
Option2: Convert B into a category of A
Option3: Merge them into a single entity type (or table)
Option4: Make A a weak entity type of B
CorrectAnswer: Merge them into a single entity type (or table)
Explanation: Because each A corresponds to exactly one B and vice versa, their attributes can be combined in one type.

Subject: DBMS
Question: Only members of the HOURLY_EMPLOYEE subclass can belong to a TRADE_UNION. How is this best modeled in EER?
Option1: As a derived attribute of TRADE_UNION
Option2: As a relationship between EMPLOYEE and TRADE_UNION with total participation
Option3: As a relationship type BELONGS_TO between HOURLY_EMPLOYEE and TRADE_UNION
Option4: As a multivalued attribute of EMPLOYEE
CorrectAnswer: As a relationship type BELONGS_TO between HOURLY_EMPLOYEE and TRADE_UNION
Explanation: A subclass can have its own specific relationship types that the superclass does not participate in.
